disposition_reason: Narrative review of selenium in soils, wheat and human health with secondary intake, toxicity and wheat concentration figures.
regulatory_or_exposure: p. 48: review reports US RDA 55 ug/d for men and women and Australian recommendations of 85 and 70 ug/d (men, women)
p. 49: review reports WHO and EU upper safe limits of 400 and 300 ug/adult per day and a US reference dose of 350 ug/d for a 70 kg person
p. 49: review reports chronic selenosis in Enshi County, China, with coal-contaminated soil up to 8 mg/kg and intakes up to 7 mg/d
p. 48: review estimates Australian mean intake around 75 ug/d
non_numeric_findings: Global adult intake ranges from 7 ug/d in Keshan disease areas to 5000 ug/d in Chinese selenosis areas, per the review (p. 49).
Finland domestic cereal selenium was 0.01 mg/kg or less before 1984 fertilization; spring wheat now about 0.25 mg/kg (p. 52).
Selenosis symptoms named: nail thickening and cracking, hair loss, skin lesions (p. 49).
Sodium selenate is the form generally used for crop fertilization (p. 51).
